text: Maryland's plan, MOSH, lists its state-specific regulations in COMAR Title 09, Subtitle 12: employee injury and illness records (09.12.21), fall protection in steel erection (09.12.25), crane safety (09.12.26), tower crane operator certification (09.12.27), tree care (09.12.28), heat stress (09.12.32), access to information on hazardous and toxic substances (09.12.33), field sanitation (09.12.36) and personnel platforms on cranes (09.12.38). The same MOSH page lists Maryland supplements to federal standards, including 29 CFR 1926.651 (excavations), 29 CFR 1926.1201 to 1213 (confined spaces in construction), 29 CFR 1926.62 (lead) and Subpart CC (cranes). The excavation amendments keep the federal 5 ft trench rule and add that protective system records (tabulated data, designs) are kept at the jobsite (see Maryland's trench card); MOSH adopted the federal confined space in construction rule by reference effective January 2, 2017 and repealed the old state rule (COMAR 09.12.35); MOSH's list entry for that supplement links to the federal Subpart AA text itself and the adoption page names no Maryland change, so the federal rule applies as written (read 2026-11-21).
title: Maryland: MOSH-specific rules and supplements to the federal trench rule
topic: State safety plan: who enforces and what differs

text: Maryland (MOSH) uses the federal excavation rule: a protective system from 5 feet unless the trench is entirely in stable rock (29 CFR 1926.652). Maryland amends 1926.652 on records: the tabulated data used for a protective system, a slope design, the manufacturer's data and any approval to deviate from it, and an engineer's design are kept at the jobsite while the system is being built and after that until it is no longer used; then they may be kept off site but available to the Commissioner of Labor and Industry on request (Maryland amendments to 1926.652(b)(4)(iii), (c)(2)(iii), (c)(4)(iii)). Confined space in construction is the federal rule, 29 CFR 1926 Subpart AA, adopted by reference effective January 2, 2017, with no Maryland change found (MOSH adoption page and supplement list, read 2026-11-21).
title: Maryland trench rule: federal 5 feet, plus protective system records kept at the jobsite
topic: State safety plan: trench and excavation
source: MOSH, Maryland amendments to 29 CFR 1926.652; MOSH-specific standards list

text: Twenty-one states run their own OSHA plan for private construction crews. A plan must be at least as effective as federal OSHA's confined space in construction rule (29 CFR 1926 Subpart AA) and may be stricter, so name the plan as the source. Use only the line for the job's state. As checked by 2026-11-21. Uses the federal rule, no state change found: Alaska (8 AAC 61.1010(c)), Indiana (from Feb 4, 2016), Iowa (875 IAC 26.1), Kentucky (803 KAR 2:445), Maryland (by reference from Jan 2, 2017), Michigan (Part 35, except as amended), Minnesota, New Mexico, South Carolina (from Aug 28, 2015), Tennessee, Utah, Vermont (Vt. rule 24-050-003), Virginia, Wyoming (WY OSHA chapter 27). Vermont also keeps its own air contaminant table for general industry (CO 35 ppm over 8 hours); whether it reaches construction is not confirmed: ask VOSHA. Not on the plan's unique list, so taken as federal: Arizona, Nevada, North Carolina, Hawaii (not confirmed). Own rule, each has its own card: California (8 CCR 1950 to 1962, amended January 1, 2026, stricter CO limit), Washington (chapter 296-809, all industries), Oregon (437-002-0146; supervisor signs, not initials).
title: State OSHA plans and confined space: which plan states use federal Subpart AA, which have their own rule
topic: Confined space rules: which states follow federal OSHA
